what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no votes on the FY23 school budget, which the School Committee had already approved, and heard it as an informational presentation.
The superintendent and business manager said the recommended school budget increase is driven by contractual increases, health insurance and the transportation contract.

The town manager presented general government, technology, health, unclassified, debt and revised capital items, including a large health and sanitation assessment increase from a census-based formula.
Members asked for more detailed school budget breakouts, trends and comparables; the chair proposed revisiting the expected level of detail after Town Meeting.
The committee added the quarterly financial report, the Monty Tech report and the warrant report to next Wednesday's virtual meeting.

why_it_matters: The school budget, the largest part of the town's spending, reached the Finance Committee only after the School Committee had approved it, so the committee's advice on it comes late in the process.

Several school costs rise or fall with outside funds, among them one-year COVID grants, state aid under Chapter 70 and the circuit breaker reimbursement, and the state budget is not final, so the share the town budget (mostly taxes) must cover can change before Town Meeting votes.
